# FileShed Individual Contributor License Agreement

**Version 1.1 — 2026-08-01**

*Derived from the Apache Software Foundation's Individual Contributor License Agreement (V2.2), restated in plain
English, with the beneficiary named in section 1.*

Thank you for contributing to FileShed. This agreement sets out the terms under which contributions are accepted. It
exists so the project holds clear, unambiguous rights to everything inside it — enough to keep releasing FileShed as
free software under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0, and enough to offer it under other terms where that
sustains the work.

**You keep the copyright in everything you write.** This is a license, not an assignment. You grant rights alongside
the ones you keep; you do not hand them over.

You accept this agreement by signing it on your first pull request. It covers that contribution and every one after it.

## 1. Definitions

**"You"** means the individual who owns the copyright in a Contribution, or a legal entity authorized by that owner,
accepting this agreement.

**"Christopher"** means Christopher S. Case, and his successors and assigns. Every grant below runs to Christopher,
which is what allows the rights to travel intact if FileShed later moves into a company, foundation, or other entity.

**"Contribution"** means any original work of authorship — code, documentation, design, tests, translations,
configuration, or anything else — that You intentionally Submit for inclusion in FileShed.

**"Submit"** means sending a Contribution to Christopher or to the FileShed project by any means: a pull request, an
issue, a patch on a mailing list, a message in a chat channel, or anything comparable. Communication conspicuously
marked "Not a Contribution" is excluded.

**"FileShed"** means the FileShed project — self-hosted, multi-user file hosting, inspired by cloud file management
tools like Dropbox or Google Drive — together with any work it forms part of or that is derived from it.

## 2. Copyright license

That license includes the right to license and sublicense Your Contribution **under any license terms**, including

Two commitments run the other way:

- Anything already published under the AGPL-3.0 stays available under the AGPL-3.0. Released versions cannot be pulled

## 4. What you are promising

By Submitting a Contribution, You represent that:

- The Contribution is Your original work, or You otherwise have the right to submit it under these terms.
- You are legally entitled to grant the licenses above. If Your employer has rights to work You produce, You have

To submit work that is not Your original creation, send it separately from Your own Contributions, state its source

If You later discover that any of these representations was wrong about something You already submitted, say so — open

You are not expected to provide support for Your Contributions, and You may stop at any time.

Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, Contributions are provided **as is**, without warranty of

Nothing here obligates anyone to use, merge, or ship Your Contribution. Whether a Contribution is accepted is a
separate decision from this agreement.

## Signing

The first time you open a pull request, a bot comments asking you to sign. Reply with exactly:

> I have read the CLA Document and I hereby sign the CLA

Your GitHub username and that pull request are recorded in a signature file on the `cla-signatures` branch of this
repository. You sign once — every later pull request from the same account is covered automatically. If the check
does not pick up an existing signature, comment `recheck` to run it again.
